course.title: Introduction to AI
course.description: Learn the fundamentals of artificial intelligence

steps.title: Welcome to AI
steps.content:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is the simulation of human intelligence in machines that are programmed to think and learn. AI systems can perform tasks that typically require human intelligence, such as:

• Visual perception
• Speech recognition
• Decision-making
• Language translation

In this course, we'll explore the fundamental concepts of AI and how it's transforming our world.

steps.title: History of AI
steps.content:
The concept of artificial intelligence dates back to ancient history, but the field as we know it began in 1956 at the Dartmouth Conference.

Key milestones:
• 1950: Alan Turing proposes the Turing Test
• 1956: Term 'Artificial Intelligence' coined
• 1997: Deep Blue defeats world chess champion
• 2011: IBM Watson wins Jeopardy!
• 2016: AlphaGo defeats Go world champion
• 2022: ChatGPT revolutionizes conversational AI

steps.title: Types of AI
steps.content:
AI can be categorized in several ways:

**By Capability:**
• Narrow AI (ANI): Specialized in one area
• General AI (AGI): Human-level intelligence
• Super AI (ASI): Surpasses human intelligence

**By Functionality:**
• Reactive Machines: Basic AI that reacts to inputs
• Limited Memory: Can use past experiences
• Theory of Mind: Understands emotions
• Self-Aware: Has consciousness

Currently, all existing AI systems are Narrow AI.

steps.title: What is Machine Learning?
steps.content:
Machine Learning (ML) is a subset of AI that enables systems to learn and improve from experience without being explicitly programmed.

Instead of following pre-written rules, ML algorithms:
• Identify patterns in data
• Make decisions based on those patterns
• Improve their performance over time

Think of it like teaching a child to recognize animals - you show them examples, and they learn to identify new ones on their own.

steps.title: Types of Machine Learning
steps.content:
There are three main types of machine learning:

**1. Supervised Learning**
• Learns from labeled examples
• Like learning with a teacher
• Used for: Classification, Regression

**2. Unsupervised Learning**
• Finds patterns in unlabeled data
• Like exploring on your own
• Used for: Clustering, Dimensionality reduction

**3. Reinforcement Learning**
• Learns through trial and error
• Like learning to play a game
• Used for: Game playing, Robotics, Autonomous systems

modules.title: Neural Networks
modules.description: Understanding neural networks and deep learning

steps.title: What are Neural Networks?
steps.content:
Neural networks are computing systems inspired by the biological neural networks in our brains.

**Key Components:**
• Neurons (Nodes): Process and transmit information
• Connections (Edges): Link neurons together
• Weights: Determine connection strength
• Activation Functions: Decide if a neuron 'fires'

Just like our brain uses billions of neurons to process information, artificial neural networks use layers of artificial neurons to learn patterns and make decisions.

steps.title: How Neural Networks Learn
steps.content:
Neural networks learn through a process called training:

**1. Forward Propagation**
• Input data flows through the network
• Each layer processes and transforms the data
• Final layer produces an output

**2. Calculate Error**
• Compare output to expected result
• Measure how wrong the prediction was

**3. Backpropagation**
• Send error backward through network
• Adjust weights to reduce error
• Repeat until network improves

This is like learning to throw darts - you adjust your aim based on where previous throws landed.
